chapter: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
title: Ben Webster takes Budd's place and returns to Kansas City
summary: Ben replaced Budd with Eugene Coy, outplayed him when Budd was with George E. Lee, and came home to Kansas City.

bands.name: Eugene Coy and His Happy Black Aces

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: How did Ben get over there in Kansas City? Now Ben lived in Kansas City --
Ben's home was Kansas City. Ben Webster's Lester's home.
And he'd gone away. Now when you --
You met Ben Webster down where?
Oh, I never told you about this.
After I had shown him the scale and everything, and left --
Oh, Amarillo, Texas. That's what I want to find out.

That was in Amarillo. And about eight months, six or eight months later, when I left to come back to Dallas to join the -- Jesse Stone at the first black night club, Ben had taken my place with Eugene Coy playing tenor saxophone.

And I ran into him when I was with George E. Lee, because I haven't got to when I joined George E. Lee, back in Oklahoma, and Ben came up to where I was working to show me how great he could play the saxophone, and this cat like to blew me off the stand.
And so finally Ben came back to Kansas City.
Because Ben's mother was a school teacher in Kansas City.
